results: 1. Detailed neuro-ophthalmic and neurological examination, including ocular motility, ptosis fatigability, orbicularis oculi strength, limb strength, reflexes, and pupils
cranial nerve examination: bilateral ophthalmoparesis with severe limitation of extraocular movements and right exotropia; ptosis improved
limb strength (MRC) examination: normal
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
sustained upgaze fatigability test: no fatigable droop
ocular motility examination: full in all directions
pupil examination (size, light reaction): equal and reactive
limb and neck power: normal
2. Ice-pack test applied to each drooping eyelid
ice-pack test: POSITIVE
3. Serum acetylcholine-receptor antibodies
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: acetylcholine receptor antibodies strongly positive, 10.32 nmol/L
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: 10.32 nmol/L (normal <0.50) - strongly POSITIVE
4. Serum MuSK and LRP4 antibodies
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: acetylcholine receptor antibodies strongly positive, 10.32 nmol/L
anti-MuSK antibodies: negative
5. Repetitive nerve stimulation of facial and proximal limb muscles
repetitive nerve stimulation: decremental response
6. Single-fiber electromyography with jitter measurement
single-fibre EMG: normal jitter
7. Serum creatine kinase, aldolase, lactate, and electrolytes
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
creatine kinase: normal
creatine kinase and lactate: normal
8. MRI of the brain and orbits with contrast
MRI orbits: SEVERE THINNING of all extraocular muscles; exotropia of the right eye
MRI brain with contrast: no lesion, no cranial nerve enhancement
9. Electromyography and nerve-conduction studies
nerve conduction studies: normal
needle electromyography: normal

whole exome sequencing: no pathogenic variant

DIAGNOSIS: AChR-antibody–positive autoimmune ocular myasthenia gravis with chronic extraocular-muscle atrophy

ALTERNATIVE 1: Chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia due to a mitochondrial myopathy

ALTERNATIVE 2: Thyroid-associated orbitopathy

ALTERNATIVE 3: Oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy or another hereditary myopathy
